rounds.text: Triliance Polymers Ltd demonstrates extraordinary long-term profit compounding that vastly outpaces its industry, evidenced by a 25% compounded profit growth over 10 years, a 68% growth over 5 years, and a 47% growth over 3 years [E15, E16, E17], easily crushing the sector median profit growth of 16.3% [E62]. This elite operational scaling is further reinforced by a Return on Assets of 3.92%, which triples the sector benchmark of 1.37% [E8]. The stock has been heavily battered down to just 19% of the way up its 52-week range [E5], creating an extreme mismatch between its historical compounding capability and its current depressed valuation at a microcap market capitalization of ₹ 21.4 Cr [E3]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth dropped by -32% [E18], return on equity remains modest at 5% for the last year [E23], and the price-to-earnings ratio sits at an elevated 92.8x [E1].

Conceded: compounded profit growth over 10, 5, and 3 years reaches 25%, 68%, and 47% [E15, E16, E17], and the asset efficiency boasts an ROA of 3.92% versus the sector's 1.37% [E8]. However, the bull's framing of a "battered down" stock at 19% of its 52-week range [E5] ignores that this collapse directly accompanies a severe -32% drop in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E18]. This abrupt contraction confirms that expectations are not merely depressed, but actively collapsing alongside decelerating earnings [E56]. Furthermore, citing a microcap valuation of ₹ 21.4 Cr [E3] alongside a towering P/E of 92.8x [E1]—which nearly quintuples the sector benchmark of 20.32x [E6]—highlights an extreme pricing disconnect rather than a bargain. This inflated multiple is completely unjustified given a multi-year median ROE of 0% over 10 years, 1% over 5 years, and 3% over 3 years [E20, E21, E22], culminating in a low 2.71% ROE over the last 3 years [E52]. Finally, the signal engine confirms that price growth has recently outpaced profit growth by 6% [E47], proving that valuation remains dangerously ahead of actual delivery despite the recent price drop [E5].
